ai.description: This snake reaches 1 meter in length. It has a yellowish body with dark, broad, rhomboid crossbands and a compressed, oar-like tail. The head is large with a distinctively notched upper jaw.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hydrophis ornatus* is best identified by its distinctly compressed, deep body and a series of large, dark, rhomboidal dorsal blotches that often connect into a jagged band.
ai.habitat: The Ornate Reef Sea Snake inhabits shallow, coastal tropical waters of the Indian subcontinent, typically frequenting coral reefs and muddy, sediment-rich sea bottoms.
ai.behavior: The Ornate Reef Sea Snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for bottom-dwelling fish and crustaceans among coral reefs and sandy substrates under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis ornatus* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young. They typically produce litters of 2–17 offspring, with breeding occurring primarily from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hydrophis ornatus* occurs in coastal waters along the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting shallow marine environments and estuaries across the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea.
